title: 30. Utilization of experiential learning courses to enhance knowledge and workforce readiness of animal science students.
content:
Abstract
The livestock production industry plays a critical role in Hawai’i’s agricultural economy, with the beef cattle industry ranking second among agricultural commodities in the state. However, nationally and in Hawai’i, college students are entering animal science programs with no prior knowledge or hands-on experience in livestock production. To address this, five experiential learning short-courses throughout the production year were created. Additionally, a month-long immersive learning course at The Ohio State University in meat science and extension exposed students to hands-on livestock and the meat industries experience. Student participants were asked to complete both a pre- and post-training survey regarding their knowledge and perceived skills in the respective areas, as well as a reflection at the end of each course. The experiential learning curriculum includes courses in calving management, grazing management, artificial insemination (AI) management, weaning management, and reproductive technologies including ultrasound training. The hands-on portion of the workshops was shown to be the most beneficial component to the students. Student knowledge increased in the different techniques and sustainable agricultural practices (P < 0.05), industry standards (P < 0.05), and agricultural tools beneficial for livestock production (P < 0.05) throughout all experiential learning opportunities. The month-long immersive learning experience was found to be the most effective for the students, as it allowed them to better understand the meat science industry (P < 0.01), understand the different USDA Carcass grading standards (P < 0.05), and assigning USDA quality grades to carcasses (P < 0.0001). Along with the increased knowledge, these students were also able to gain confidence in communicating the topic of meat science with individuals of various communities (P < 0.05) which is essential in extension education. Short-course experiential learning opportunities are a way to enhance hands-on experience for animal science students and deepen their understanding of current industry standards. Expanding experiential learning short-courses to additional students and animal industries will strengthen workforce preparedness, promote cross-sector skill building, and amplify long-term program impact.
